title: Midnight shift: autoscale observations + SLO annotations
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures notes from the midnight SRE shift (2027-05-05 22:00 UTC -> 2027-05-06 06:00 UTC). Focus: unusual autoscale behavior in us-west1, short-lived p99 latency spikes for hosted inference, SLO annotations and immediate handoff items for day shift. Informal notes + decisions + follow-ups.

Shift leads:
- Primary: Aditi Menon (oncall)
- Secondary: Ethan Park
- Incident comms: Leila Gomez

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Observed repeated short p99 tail spikes (~200–400ms extra per request) between 2027-05-06 00:15–01:10 UTC affecting ~6% of requests to hosted-inference-us-west1. Availability not impacted (errors remained <0.1%), but latency SLO (p99 <= 350ms target) breached twice for ~12 minutes total.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): transient KV cache eviction anomalies coupled with an aggressive scale-down step that removed a hot pod mid-prefix-warm period. Autoscaler policy allowed scale-down within 90s of pod creation; this interacted poorly with our continuous-batching prefix warm-up, increasing KV cache miss amplification.
- Mitigation performed: temporarily raised min-replicas for us-west1 pool from 6 -> 8 and disabled aggressive scale-down window. Reverted after stabilization planning (see actions).

Timeline (detailed):
- 00:12 UTC: first p99 spike alerted by observability rule (p99 hosted-inference-us-west1 > 400ms for 2m).
- 00:15 UTC: oncall bridge opened, phone page to primary.
- 00:17 UTC: quick correlation: request volume steady; error budget not consumed. Traces show increased tail due to KV-lookups falling back to remote store (higher latency).
- 00:22 UTC: infra team noticed scale-down events for 2 pods in us-west1 approximately 30s before spike onset (autoscaler logs).
- 00:28 UTC: applied temp mitigation: set pool.min_replicas=8 and autoscaler.scale_down_grace=300s.
- 00:35 UTC: p99 returns below threshold.
- 00:45 UTC: another short spike after a deploy / rollout activity from a separate team (deploy window 00:42–00:43 UTC) — likely related (rollout caused short warm-cache window + scale decisions).
- 01:05 UTC: confirmed no errors and p99 stable for 20m. Bridge closed at 01:20 UTC. Handed off to day shift with follow-ups.

Observations and evidence collected:
- Traces: sample traces show initial token generation path waiting on KV cache miss and a synchronous fallback to remote KVS; extra 150–350ms per affected request.
- Autoscaler logs: scale-downs initiated by controller within 90–110s after pod creation in several instances. Policy config shows scale_down_delay_seconds=90 (current, pre-change).
- Deploy timeline: a canary rollout from infra-team overlapped with the event window (canary job SLS-672).
- Heap and kernel logs: no OOMs, no GPU process restarts. CPU/IO within normal ranges.

Immediate mitigations taken (temporary):
- Bumped min_replicas(us-west1) 6->8 (Aditi; 00:28 UTC).
- Increased scale_down_grace 90->300s (Aditi; 00:29 UTC).
- Rolled back an in-progress non-critical canary (infra-team) after confirmation with on-call (Leila; 00:46 UTC).

Longer-term remediation plan (action items):
1) Autoscaler policy review and test harness (owner: Marcus Chen; due: 2027-05-14):
   - Reduce sensitivity to short-lived pods created for canaries; add cooling window tuned to prefix warm-up distribution.
   - Add unit and e2e tests to simulate prefix-warm scenarios.
   - Jira: SRE-578 (linked).
2) KV cache fallbacks: async warming + circuit-breaker (owner: Ethan Park; due: 2027-05-21):
   - Implement async pre-warming for new pods for top-100 prefixes per pool.
   - Introduce a short-lived local warming cache plus a circuit-breaker to avoid synchronous remote hits during warm-up.
   - Jira: SRE-581.
3) Rollout coordination: deploy gating for high-traffic windows (owner: Leila Gomez; due: 2027-05-10):
   - Add policy to avoid starting canaries during midnight-window (00:00–02:00 UTC) for high-impact pools.
   - Add slack bridge automated notifier when a canary overlaps with high-latency risk windows.
4) Observability: add spike context to p99 alerts (owner: Aditi Menon; due: 2027-05-09):
   - Alert should include recent scale_events and recent deploy IDs to reduce MTTR.

SLO snapshot (pre/post-incident):
- SLO: hosted-inference-us-west1 latency p99 target <= 350ms (rolling 30d).
- Current 30d: 99.2% met.
- Window 2027-05-01 -> 2027-05-06: small dip to 98.9% due to two short breaches (today).
- Error budget remaining: ~12.3% (still healthy).
- Notes: incident did not consume much of the budget but highlights tail-risk from autoscale interactions.

Runbook updates suggested:
- Add a quick-check section: "If p99 spike + no traffic surge -> check recent scale_down events and recent deploys" (owner: Aditi; due: 2027-05-08).
- Document how to temporarily change min_replicas safely from console and rollback steps.

On-call handoff (to day shift):
- Summary to pass along: watch for any more p99 regressions in us-west1 between 00:00–04:00 UTC. If p99 > 400ms for >=2m, open bridge and escalate to infra.
- Items in handoff checklist:
  - Verify min_replicas remains at 8 only until remediation is in place; schedule automatic revert to 6 after autoscaler policy change merged.
  - Follow up on SRE-578 and SRE-581 progress during weekly SRE sync (Fri 15:00 PT).
  - Confirm infra deploys are gated for midnight window.

Unresolved questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Why did autoscaler choose to scale down pods so soon after creation? (logs show decision based on node-level metrics; need controller debug info).
- Are there any hidden interactions between canary job labeling and our warm-up heuristics?
- Would a short-lived local warming layer reduce synchronous remote KVS calls without increasing memory footprint significantly?

Notes to product and infra partners:
- Infra: please confirm whether the autoscaler controller has known regressions related to scale decision timing (GH PRs referenced in linked artifacts).
- Product: this is low customer impact now, but repeated tail-risk can degrade user experience for LLM apps; consider gating feature rollouts in high-traffic pools.

Action items recap (short):
- Marcus: autoscaler policy + test harness (SRE-578).
- Ethan: KV cache async warm circuit-breaker design doc + proof-of-concept (SRE-581).
- Leila: gating policy for canaries during midnight window; add slack automation.
- Aditi: runbook quick-check & alert context enhancements.

Meeting / sync requests:
- Schedule 30m wartime retro with infra and serving-runtime next Tue (2027-05-11 16:00 PT) to go over the interplay between rollout cadence and autoscale settings.
- Add agenda item to weekly SRE sync (Fri) for progress updates on SRE-578 and SRE-581.

Misc notes and small housekeeping:
- Observability tweak attempted during shift (Aditi) to include last-deploy-id in p99 alert. This required minor dashboard work — submitted PR GH:repo/infra-config/pull/214 (linked).
- No PagerDuty reassignments were needed; secondary covered follow-ups.

Appendix: quick links and debugging commands used during shift:
- kubectl logs --since=15m -l pool=hosted-inference-us-west1 --tail=200
- curl -s https://observability.internal/api/v1/metrics?p99=hosted-inference-us-west1
- Autoscaler event query: /internal/autoctl/events?pool=us-west1&from=2027-05-06T00:00Z&to=2027-05-06T02:00Z

If anything else pops up during the morning, ping me in #ops-bridge or oncall page.

— Aditi
